# Kyoto Spring Cultural Escape

This 3-day itinerary focuses on the serene Zen temples and refined culinary traditions of Kyoto during the peak cherry blossom season. With a total budget of $1,500 USD (approx. ¥225,000 JPY), you will experience high-end Kaiseki dining and tranquil tea ceremonies at a moderate, contemplative pace.

# Three-Day Zen and Tradition Itinerary

Day 1: Arashiyama Zen and Bamboo Groves
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Tenryu-ji_Sogenchi_Garden_2012.JPG/1200px-Tenryu-ji_Sogenchi_Garden_2012.JPG Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Tenryu-ji Temple**: Explore this head Zen temple and its 14th-century Sogenchi Garden, designed to frame the surrounding mountains.
- **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove**: Walk the ethereal path through towering bamboo stalks located immediately behind the temple grounds.
- **Traditional Tea Ceremony**: Participate in a private, meditative tea preparation at a local machiya overlooking the Hozugawa River.
Action: [Button: View Tenryu-ji Info] https://www.tenryuji.com/en/

Day 2: Higashiyama Heritage and Kaiseki Dining
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Kiyomizu-dera_in_Kyoto-r.jpg/1200px-Kiyomizu-dera_in_Kyoto-r.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Kiyomizu-dera Temple**: Visit this iconic wooden temple at sunrise to appreciate the panoramic views of Kyoto and the cherry blossoms.
- **Kodai-ji Temple**: Experience the stunning Zen gardens and "weeping" cherry trees at this temple established in 1606.
- **Authentic Kaiseki Dinner**: Enjoy a multi-course seasonal feast at a Michelin-starred establishment in the historic Gion district.
Action: [Button: Reserve Kaiseki] https://www.tableall.com/restaurant/135

Day 3: The Art of Zen Rock Gardens
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/12/Ryoanji_Temple_Kyoto_Japan.jpg/1200px-Ryoanji_Temple_Kyoto_Japan.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- **Ryoan-ji Temple**: Contemplate the world's most famous Zen rock garden, consisting of 15 stones arranged in a sea of white gravel.
- **Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)**: View the gold-leaf-covered Zen temple reflecting in the "Mirror Pond" amidst spring blooms.
- **Sannenzaka & Ninenzaka Walk**: Conclude with a slow stroll through preserved streets for traditional crafts and incense shopping.

# Local Transit and IC Card Guide

Kyoto's districts are best navigated using **ICOCA** (local) or **Suica** (standard) cards. These are "tap-and-go" cards available at any train station ticket machine.

- **Using IC Cards**: Tap the card on the luminous blue reader at ticket gates (trains) or when exiting the bus. Ensure a minimum balance of ¥500.
- **Arashiyama to Gion**: Take the JR Sagano Line from Saga-Arashiyama to Kyoto Station, then transfer to the Subway Karasuma Line or a taxi.
- **Higashiyama to Gion**: These districts are adjacent; walking via the Sannenzaka slope is the most scenic and efficient route.
- **Kyoto City Bus**: Kyoto buses have a flat fare of ¥230. Tap your IC card on the reader next to the driver only when getting off the bus.
